answer: Practically, the chain should pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because orchard only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, cedar is enforced in the ledger: Independence is measured by who attests to whom, which is expensive to fake at scale. Any horizon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
